prompt: A client receives an ARP reply from the FortiGate for a peer address, but TCP still fails. What has the capture actually proved?

choices.text: The peer is authorized by the firewall policy.
choices.feedback: Authorization is a later policy decision; ARP resolution alone does not prove it.

choices.text: The proxy-ARP range answered for that IPv4 address.
choices.feedback: Correct: the FortiGate is answering for the destination address in that range.

choices.text: The FortiSwitch blocked every alternate path.
choices.feedback: Switch isolation must be verified separately from the ARP reply.

choices.text: The return route is installed on the FortiGate.
choices.feedback: A route is not established by observing an ARP response.

prompt: With intra-VLAN blocking enabled, a same-VLAN packet enters and leaves the FortiGate on the same VLAN interface. Which control prevents the documented traffic-redirect bypass?

choices.text: Disable `allow-traffic-redirect` globally.
choices.feedback: Correct: the guide calls for disabling this redirect behavior so same-interface traffic is policy checked.

choices.text: Enable proxy ARP on every interface.
choices.feedback: Proxy ARP supplies ARP resolution; it does not control the redirect bypass.

choices.text: Change the VLAN to a routed port.
choices.feedback: Changing the interface type is not the documented control.

choices.text: Disable DHCP snooping on the switch.
choices.feedback: DHCP snooping is unrelated to the firewall policy path.

prompt: An IPv6 host cannot reach another client on a VLAN where intra-VLAN blocking is enabled. What is the most accurate first conclusion?

choices.text: The proxy-ARP pool is too small.
choices.feedback: Proxy-ARP pool sizing is an IPv4 address-range issue.

choices.text: The policy ID is not synchronized.
choices.feedback: Policy synchronization does not explain the documented IPv6 limitation.

choices.text: IPv6 client-to-client traffic is unsupported in this mode.
choices.feedback: Correct: the FortiSwitch guide explicitly documents this boundary.

choices.text: The FortiGate needs an IPv6 VIP.
choices.feedback: An IPv6 VIP is not a substitute for the unsupported intra-VLAN behavior.

prompt: A design must preserve isolation when FortiLink connectivity is lost. Which setting expresses the intended behavior?

choices.text: `set access-vlan-mode fail-open`
choices.feedback: Fail-open permits intra-VLAN traffic during the FortiLink outage.

choices.text: `set access-vlan-mode fail-close`
choices.feedback: Correct: fail-close keeps intra-VLAN traffic blocked when the FortiGate connection is lost.

choices.text: `set match-period 0`
choices.feedback: Match-period controls NAC/DPP record retention, not outage forwarding.

choices.text: `set allow-traffic-redirect enable`
choices.feedback: Enabling redirect can undermine the policy-inspection design.

prompt: A `um/query/productapi` request returns an IPS signature description. Which statement is justified?

choices.text: The signature is installed on every managed FortiGate.
choices.feedback: Package metadata does not prove device installation.

choices.text: The signature matched live traffic in the last hour.
choices.feedback: A signature lookup does not report runtime traffic matches.

choices.text: The queried signature metadata was retrieved from product data.
choices.feedback: Correct: it proves the requested metadata lookup succeeded.

choices.text: The IPS sensor references the signature in every policy.
choices.feedback: Sensor and policy attachment must be checked on the managed device.

prompt: Which target is documented for looking up a single IPS signature by ID?

choices.text: `/fgd/lookup/ency?source=ips&id=58947`
choices.feedback: Correct: this is the documented encyclopedia lookup form.

choices.text: `/pm/config/adom/root/pkg/ips/58947`
choices.feedback: This is not the documented productapi target path.

choices.text: `/sys/status/ips?id=58947`
choices.feedback: A system-status path does not perform the encyclopedia lookup.

choices.text: `/fortiguard/ips/install?signature=58947`
choices.feedback: The lookup is read-only metadata retrieval, not an install action.

prompt: A package inventory uses `limit=10` and reports more than ten signatures. What is required for a complete audit?

choices.text: Repeat the first request until it returns the same page.
choices.feedback: Repeating the same offset returns the same first page.

choices.text: Increase the FortiGate IPS engine memory.
choices.feedback: Engine memory does not control API pagination.

choices.text: Fetch subsequent pages with the correct offset.
choices.feedback: Correct: continue offsets until the reported total is covered.

choices.text: Treat the first ten signatures as representative.
choices.feedback: A sample page is not a complete package inventory.

prompt: An engineer needs to identify signatures added or removed between two IPS package releases. Which query is the best fit?

choices.text: A single signature encyclopedia lookup.
choices.feedback: A single lookup describes one signature, not a release difference.

choices.text: A package-version delta query.
choices.feedback: Correct: the documented two-version target returns package delta information.

choices.text: A managed-device reboot history query.
choices.feedback: Reboot history is unrelated to package-content comparison.

choices.text: A policy package installation preview.
choices.feedback: Install preview evaluates deployment changes, not IPS signature deltas.

prompt: The Azure Logs Ingestion API requires a `TimeGenerated` field. Which documented DCR transformation supplies it?

choices.text: `source | project-away message`
choices.feedback: This removes a field but does not create the required timestamp.

choices.text: `source | extend TimeGenerated = todatetime(logtime) | project-away logtime`
choices.feedback: Correct: it converts logtime into TimeGenerated and removes the temporary field.

choices.text: `source | summarize count() by TimeGenerated`
choices.feedback: This assumes TimeGenerated already exists in the source payload.

choices.text: `source | extend logtime = now() | project message`
choices.feedback: This renames no field into the required schema.

prompt: Which Azure permission is specified for the application registration on the Data Collection Rule?

choices.text: Log Analytics Reader
choices.feedback: Reader access alone does not grant the documented ingestion role.

choices.text: Monitoring Metrics Publisher
choices.feedback: Correct: Fortinet specifies Monitoring Metrics Publisher for the DCR.

choices.text: Storage Blob Data Contributor
choices.feedback: Blob storage access is not the Logs Ingestion API role.

choices.text: Security Reader
choices.feedback: Security Reader is not the documented DCR ingestion role.

prompt: The FortiAnalyzer output profile passes Validate and Save, but the destination table remains empty. What should be checked next?

choices.text: The FortiAnalyzer local archive retention only.
choices.feedback: Local archive retention is a separate storage path.

choices.text: The DCR/table schema and matching Log Forwarding rule.
choices.feedback: Correct: validate rule eligibility and the DCR stream/schema end to end.

choices.text: The FortiGate session pickup setting.
choices.feedback: Session pickup does not control external log forwarding.

choices.text: The FortiAnalyzer administrator password expiry.
choices.feedback: Administrator password expiry is not the first explanation for an accepted profile.

prompt: Only traffic logs arrive in Azure; event logs do not. Which boundary is most relevant?

choices.text: Each log family may require a matching Log Forwarding rule.
choices.feedback: Correct: rule filters and selected log types determine which records enter the output path.

choices.text: The DCE can ingest only traffic logs.
choices.feedback: The DCE is not inherently limited to traffic logs.

choices.text: The local Analytics database must be rebuilt.
choices.feedback: Rebuilding Analytics is unrelated to selecting log families for forwarding.

choices.text: The FortiGate must disable log compression.
choices.feedback: Log compression is not the documented cause of per-family forwarding gaps.

prompt: A NAC policy has `match-period 48`, but the device does not retain the match for 48 hours. What configuration prerequisite should be checked first?

choices.text: The FortiSwitch port speed.
choices.feedback: Port speed does not control NAC match retention.

choices.text: The policy `match-type` is set to `override`.
choices.feedback: Correct: the FortiLink guide says to switch from dynamic to override before setting match-period.

choices.text: The DHCP lease is also 48 hours.
choices.feedback: DHCP lease duration is a separate timer.

choices.text: The RADIUS server has a CoA secret.
choices.feedback: CoA secrets are unrelated to the explicit match retention field.

prompt: What does `match-period 0` mean in the documented NAC/DPP behavior?

choices.text: Expire the match immediately.
choices.feedback: Zero is not an immediate-expiry setting here.

choices.text: Retain the match indefinitely until a documented removal event.
choices.feedback: Correct: zero means indefinite retention subject to documented removal events.

choices.text: Use the DHCP lease as the retention timer.
choices.feedback: The DHCP lease is not the match-period timer.

choices.text: Retain the match for 120 days exactly.
choices.feedback: The maximum configured value is 3,072 hours; zero is not 120 days.

prompt: A switch-controller warning reports that matched NAC devices have reached 95 percent of the maximum. What does it indicate?

choices.text: A particular device's match has expired.
choices.feedback: The warning is a capacity signal, not an expiry event.

choices.text: The switch has lost its FortiLink tunnel.
choices.feedback: FortiLink loss is not what the 95-percent warning represents.

choices.text: The matched-device capacity is approaching its limit.
choices.feedback: Correct: it warns that the matched-device maximum is nearing exhaustion.

choices.text: Every NAC rule has stopped matching.
choices.feedback: A capacity warning does not prove all rules stopped evaluating.

prompt: A NAC-matched device receives the expected VLAN but not the configured QoS treatment. Which documented condition should be checked?

choices.text: The matched device is the only device on the port.
choices.feedback: Correct: the QoS enhancement is conditional on the matching device being the only device on the port.

choices.text: The switch is using a 10-Gigabit uplink.
choices.feedback: Uplink speed does not satisfy the single-device condition.

choices.text: The VLAN has a DHCP relay configured.
choices.feedback: DHCP relay is not the documented QoS prerequisite.

choices.text: The match-period is set to 120 days.
choices.feedback: Retention duration does not determine whether port QoS is applied.

prompt: An IPv6-only AP management subnet uses multicast discovery. Which FortiGate setting advertises the controller discovery multicast address?

choices.text: `set discovery-mc-addr6 <IPv6 address>`
choices.feedback: Correct: this sets the IPv6 multicast address used for AP discovery.

choices.text: `set ap-discover enable`
choices.feedback: Automatic registration is not the multicast address setting.

choices.text: `set ip6-send-adv disable`
choices.feedback: Disabling router advertisements does not configure controller multicast discovery.

choices.text: `set capwap-data-channel clear-text`
choices.feedback: Data-channel security mode is unrelated to the discovery address.

prompt: A design uses DHCPv6 to tell FortiAP where the controller is. Which option is documented?

choices.text: Option 43 with an IPv4 controller address.
choices.feedback: Option 43 is not the documented IPv6 controller discovery method here.

choices.text: Option 52 with the AC IPv6 address.
choices.feedback: Correct: DHCPv6 Option 52 carries the AC IPv6 address.

choices.text: Option 60 with the AP vendor class.
choices.feedback: Option 60 is not the specified controller-address option.

choices.text: Option 82 with the client circuit ID.
choices.feedback: Option 82 is unrelated to this FortiAP discovery mechanism.

prompt: IPv6 CAPWAP management works on a FortiGate NP6 appliance, but CAPWAP data offload is absent. What is the best interpretation?

choices.text: The AP firmware is necessarily corrupted.
choices.feedback: The documented platform caveat does not imply AP corruption.

choices.text: The IPv6 address must be removed from the AP.
choices.feedback: Removing IPv6 is not required for management to work.

choices.text: NP6/NP6lite does not support this CAPWAP offload.
choices.feedback: Correct: CAPWAP offload is supported on NP7/NP7lite, not NP6/NP6lite.

choices.text: The controller multicast address is always invalid.
choices.feedback: A working management association makes multicast-address failure less likely.

prompt: The AP is discovered and authorized, but clients in a tunnel-mode SSID cannot pass data. Which next check best separates control from data?

choices.text: Verify the CAPWAP data channel and SSID forwarding path.
choices.feedback: Correct: discovery/authorization does not prove the data tunnel and SSID path work.

choices.text: Change the DHCPv6 Option 52 value first.
choices.feedback: Option 52 is relevant when discovery is failing, not after authorization.

choices.text: Increase the controller multicast scope.
choices.feedback: Multicast scope is not the first check for an established AP with data failure.

choices.text: Assume the IPv6 management ping proves client forwarding.
choices.feedback: A management ping proves reachability only, not client traffic forwarding.

prompt: A NetFlow exporter is configured but FortiNAC Network Sessions remains empty. Which destination contract should be verified?

choices.text: TCP/443 to the FortiNAC GUI.
choices.feedback: The GUI port does not receive the documented flow export.

choices.text: UDP flow export to the FortiNAC IP on port 2055.
choices.feedback: Correct: the FortiNAC guide specifies its IP address and listener port 2055.

choices.text: UDP/720 broadcasts between HA peers.
choices.feedback: UDP/720 is used in a different product's HA discovery context.

choices.text: TCP/22 from the FortiNAC appliance.
choices.feedback: SSH reachability does not prove NetFlow export delivery.

prompt: What is the strongest limitation to remember when using NetFlow as profiling evidence?

choices.text: It contains the full application payload for every session.
choices.feedback: NetFlow does not provide full application payload.

choices.text: It proves which user saw a decrypted page.
choices.feedback: Flow metadata cannot prove the exact page content seen by a user.

choices.text: It is flow metadata, not packet payload inspection.
choices.feedback: Correct: flow records summarize traffic metadata and depend on exporter fields.

choices.text: It automatically registers every observed endpoint.
choices.feedback: Profiling and automatic registration are separate outcomes.

prompt: Network Sessions shows the expected flow tuple, but the device profiling rule does not match. What is the best next step?

choices.text: Inspect Network Traffic Method criteria against the received flow attributes.
choices.feedback: Correct: received sessions prove collection; the rule criteria are the next boundary.

choices.text: Change the collector port from 2055 to 443.
choices.feedback: Changing the port would likely stop the working flow feed.

choices.text: Rebuild the FortiNAC database immediately.
choices.feedback: A database rebuild is disproportionate without evidence of corruption.

choices.text: Assume the exporter has stopped sending records.
choices.feedback: The visible sessions contradict the claim that the exporter stopped.

prompt: A device matches the Network Traffic Method but remains rogue. Which distinction matters?

choices.text: NetFlow v9 cannot create host records.
choices.feedback: NetFlow version does not explain registration behavior by itself.

choices.text: The profile match and registration action are separate decisions.
choices.feedback: Correct: inspect whether the rule is configured for automatic or manual registration.

choices.text: The FortiNAC IP address must be public.
choices.feedback: The collector can receive flows on an internal address.

choices.text: Every matching rule registers devices automatically.
choices.feedback: Automatic registration is a rule setting, not a universal consequence.

prompt: Two endpoint fingerprint records show the same MAC and port but different operating systems. What event should be expected?

choices.text: Device Fingerprint Changed.
choices.feedback: Correct: the guide describes this event for differing OS fingerprints on the same MAC/port.

choices.text: RADIUS Accounting Stop.
choices.feedback: Accounting Stop is a RADIUS session event, not the fingerprint-change event.

choices.text: FortiLink Member Down.
choices.feedback: FortiLink state is unrelated to the endpoint identity records.

choices.text: Host Registration Timeout.
choices.feedback: The event is not defined as a registration timeout.
